messages:
jess: putting this here — new eu-west1 nodepool provisioned by infra CI; nodes come up with taint `gpu:reserved=true` and no `redwood/gpu-type` label. ~12 pods pending with nodeSelector gpu=rtx, most show ContainerCreating or ImagePullBackOff.

calvin: is this the pool from last night's infra rollout? pinging @nora and @alan. any idea if the driver daemonset ran?

sre-bot: autoscaler: created nodegroup 'euw-gpu-pooled-2026-03' (size 6) — taints applied: gpu:reserved=true; node join events observed at 2026-03-15T02:14:10Z.

nora: quick check — these nodes often join before the driver DS finishes. can you run `kubectl get nodes -l cloud.k8s.io/name=euw-gpu-pooled-2026-03 -o wide` and paste a node name?

jess: node example: euw-node-3. here's a snippet from a failing pod:

```
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/training-job-1 to euw-node-3
  Warning FailedMount 2m    kubelet            MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "nvidia-device" : hostPath type check failed: /dev/nvidia0 does not exist on the node
```

jess: also saw kubelet logs with "nvidia: module not found" — looks like driver DS didn't run or failed due to kernel mismatch.

alan: that fits a known race: node registers, kubelet reports Ready, but the driver daemonset hasn't created host devices yet. quick mitigation: remove the taint on one node so pods can land where drivers are present, or run a restart of the driver DS. longer term: infra should add a node-init probe that only removes the `provisioning` taint after drivers confirmed.

calvin: proposed immediate plan: 1) remove taint on a single node (to let a couple pods start) 2) restart driver DS (`kubectl rollout restart ds/nvidia-driver-installer -n kube-system`) 3) wait for device nodes to appear 4) run descheduler job to rebalance small pods off the driver-less nodes 5) re-apply taint. ok?

nora: also note: saw CNI flaps in `dmesg` on two of these nodes — possible NIC/MTU mismatch when they were provisioned. please check `dmesg | grep -i eth` if pods still show networking issues after device fix.

jess: will try the taint removal on euw-node-3 and restart the DS now.

jess: done on euw-node-3 — `kubectl taint nodes euw-node-3 gpu:reserved-` and `kubectl rollout restart ds/nvidia-driver-installer -n kube-system`. pods are transitioning to Running :eyes:

calvin: great. i'll schedule descheduler run in ~5m to sweep and rebalance. leaving a short maintenance window to avoid churn on long training jobs. :thumbsup:

alan: long-term action items: (a) add driver-ready nodeCondition / taint gating, (b) make infra apply `redwood/gpu-type` label during provisioning, (c) ensure CNI config consistency across AZs.

jess: noted. i'll open a follow-up ticket with the logs and apply the above recommendations. thanks all.
